title: QuickCascade starterpacks — streaming-first SDK samples & retry patterns
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Goal: Ship a compact, opinionated set of starter projects and cookbook snippets that demonstrate production-ready streaming ergonomics, robust retry/backoff patterns, and minimal-ops integration across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (HTTP server), and a CLI.

Why: Existing sample packs are comprehensive but large; customers often ask for a tiny 'launchpad' that shows best practices for token streaming, client-side incremental rendering, idempotent retries, and server batching with KV-cache hints. This ticket produces a cohesive set that teams can drop into a repo and adapt quickly.

Deliverables:
- nextjs-streaming-starter: Next.js 14 demo with streaming UI (token-by-token render), reconnection/resume example, and client-side backoff for transient errors.
- fastapi-proxy-starter: FastAPI example implementing request multiplexing, simple request coalescing, idempotency key handling, and server-side KV cache header examples.
- go-miniserver-starter: Minimal Go HTTP server showcasing concurrency-safe streaming response handling, graceful shutdown, and backpressure control.
- cli-tokstream: Small cross-platform CLI sample (Go) that demonstrates streaming responses, SIGINT-safe checkpointing, and resumable downloads.
- cookbook-snippets.md: Compact snippets for exponential backoff + jitter, idempotency key design, streaming parsers (JSONL / SSE), and unit/integration test harness for recorded responses.

Non-goals: Full tutorial ecosystem, heavy SDK reference changes, or adding new API surface areas. Focus is examples + patterns rather than SDK internals.
acceptance_criteria: Each starter app builds and runs locally with provided README steps
Next.js demo renders streaming tokens incrementally in <200ms per chunk on local dev for demo prompts
FastAPI sample demonstrates a simple batching endpoint that groups requests within a 10ms window and returns aggregated responses
Go server cleanly handles 100 concurrent streaming clients in local stress test without panics (CI smoke test)
CLI supports resume via idempotency key and shows example flows in README
Cookbook includes at least 5 practical snippets with explanation and test harness examples
PRs include unit tests or smoke scripts and link to design doc; reviewers sign off (PM + SDK lead + DevEx)
tasks: Write Next.js streaming demo (TS) with sample UI and minimal CSS
Implement FastAPI proxy sample with batching toggle and idempotency demo
Build Go HTTP server sample with streaming flush and graceful shutdown
Create Go CLI example showcasing streaming and resume semantics
Author cookbook-snippets.md and include common retry primitives + test harness
Create CI smoke scripts that run each sample for basic operation
Write README / quickstart for each starter explaining tradeoffs and recommended prod knobs
Open PRs, collect feedback, iterate on ergonomics and docs
notes:
Design doc: https://docs.redwood-inference.internal/SDK-QuickCascade (internal)
Initial proto and sketches in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qk-demo-examples
Design decisions: favor small, opinionated examples over exhaustive coverage; show both client- and server-side retry patterns.
Runtime knobs to highlight: streaming chunk size, client read timeouts, reconnect jitter, server batching window, and KV-cache hint headers.
Testing: record golden transcripts for the Next.js UI and use recorded responses in CI for deterministic rendering tests.
